message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical, Chemical, and Nuclear Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, so it does not readily accept an electron) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 g cm⁻³) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Specific heat (gas) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Diffusivity | Extremely high (≈0.1 cm² s⁻¹ at 25 °C) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ (≈0.18 g L⁻¹) |
| **Chemical Behavior** | Bond type | Diatomic (H₂) |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, reacts with halogens, oxidizes to water or oxides |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (molecular) |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (HF) or base (H⁻) depending on partner |
| | Combustion | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, releases ~286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Flame temperature | ~2,800 °C (when burning in air) |
| | Flammability limits | Lower limit 4 % vol, upper limit 75 % vol in air |
| **Nuclear Properties** | Proton number | 1 |
| | Neutron number | 0 (protium), 1 (deuterium), 2 (tritium) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 0 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.7928 µ_N (protium), 0 (deuterium), 5.5857 µ_N (tritium) |
| | Half‑life (tritium) | 12.32 years |
| | Decay mode (tritium) | β⁻ decay to helium‑3 |
| **Applications & Uses** | Fuel | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant (LH₂) |
| | Industrial | Production of ammonia (Haber process), refining of petroleum, synthesis of organic compounds |
| | Energy storage | Metal hydrides, polymer electrolyte membranes |
| | Scientific research | Calibration standards, neutron sources (via tritium), quantum chemistry studies |
| | Environmental | Clean combustion produces only water vapor |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: lowest density, highest diffusivity, and very low boiling/melting points.
- **Highly reactive**: forms a wide variety of compounds (hydrides, acids, bases, organohydrogens).
- **Isotopic diversity**: deuterium and tritium have distinct nuclear properties and applications (e.g., nuclear fusion research, radiolabeling).
- **Energy relevance**: central to clean‑energy technologies (fuel cells, hydrogen economy) and rocket propulsion.
- **Safety**: flammable in a wide concentration range; requires careful handling and storage.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
